entry.dc:title: Combined Open Pit and Underground Mining Method at Aghires Mine.
entry.dc:creator: Muste I.
entry.dc:description: After discussing the deposit, the author indicates that in a mining field of about 50 ha seam, caolinous sand was mined by using the chamber method with abandoned pillars. An extraction of 60% sand from seam II or 20% of the overall reserves from this field was reached. Following this, after having described the physical and mechanical features of the ore seams and the host rock, a safety plate was provided over the stopes and three alternatives for the open pit mining of the remaining reserves were designed.

entry.dc:title: IN-PIT MINING SYSTEMS.
entry.dc:creator: Wood J.
entry.dc:description: As open pit mining operations go deeper because of earlier exploitation of deposits with low overburden ratios and high grade seams, mine operations must now look to more highly mechanised methods for both waste and mineral recovery and for transportation out of the pit to utilisation or ultimate disposal. Although these mechanised techniques have had wide acceptance for many years in Europe and Victoria's Latrobe Valley, for the exploitation of lignite on a very large scale for pwer generation and for bauxite mining in WA and NT, their adoption to other forms of hardrock mining has only been seriously considered during the last ten years. Mechanised methods offer an economic solution to the exploitation of mineral deposits with higher overburden ratios than have been considered feasible in the past and in pits up to 250 metres deep. Their successful application depends on a system approach to the selection of each element involved in the new mining process.

entry.dc:title: INCO'S NEW OPEN PIT DELIVERS LOW-COST NICKEL ORE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Filling the processing pipeline with lowcost mined nickel ore was Inco's main motive for developing its new Thompson open pit mine in northern Manitoba, Canada. The new pit, which mines the crown pillar of the Thompson underground mine, replaces ore that was previously railed from the Pipe open-pit, located 20 min to the south. The decision to bring the Thompson open-pit mine into production rather than rejuvenate or develop any of the other underground mines was based primarily of the fact that surface mining technology, personnel, and equipment already existed at the Pipe open pit. Mining is carried out in the pit two shifts/day operating on 45-ft benches with 25-ft berms. The ultimate dimensions of the mine will be 5,100 ft along the north-south direction, 800 ft in the east-west direction, and 400 ft below surface at its deepest point.

entry.dc:title: OPTIMUM SCALE OF AN OPEN PIT OPERATION: DISCOUNT RATE AND RISK.
entry.dc:creator: Schaap W.
entry.prism:publicationName: Bulletin and Proceedings Australasian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: For a large scale open pit mining and concentrating operation on a low-grade disseminated ore body, it is possible to set an approximate lower bound on economically feasible operating scales and an approximate upper bound on economically desirable scales. The effects of infrastructural costs and the addition of a risk premium to form the discount rate for planning purposes are considered theoretically and by worked example.

entry.dc:title: SANDWICH BELT HIGH ANGLE CONVEYORS - HAC: EVOLUTION TO DATE.
entry.dc:creator: Dos Santos J.
entry.dc:description: Sandwich belt conveyors may be used to transport materials at high angles, to 90 degree , while maintaining the most positive features of conventional conveyors. The present discussion deals with the evolution and development of sandwich belt high angle conveyors (HACs) to satisfy the operational requirements of the open pit mining and materials handling industries. The relationship between conveying angle and hugging pressure by the cover belt is developed mathematically. The vertical-radius-of-curvature constraints are discussed in detail, and the constraint equations are developed. Criteria for development are established as basis for the evolutionary development of the latest sandwich belt HACs. Finally, design features of the first large-scale prototype and the latest commercial HAC units, one in coal, the other in an open pit copper mine, are described.

entry.dc:title: Principal Lines of Development of the Coal Industry in the Twelfth Five Year Plan Period.
entry.dc:creator: Shchadov M.
entry.dc:description: In the 11th FYP period 3537. 7 Mt of coal have been mined in the USSR. The annual output in 1985 was 718 Mt, i. e. 8. 7 Mt more than in 1980. Open pit mining increased by 25. 1 Mt, i. e. by 13. 2%, and its share in the total output rose from 36. 8 to 41. 1%, mainly due to the development of the Kuznetsk, Kansk-Achinsk and Ekibastuz basins. There were many shortcomings which are noted. By 1990 the plan envisages an in output in output to 780-800 Mt. Many mines will be exhausted, especially in the Donetsk basin, therefore deeper seams would have to be developed. The main increase in the output of coal is envisaged in Siberia and the Far East. By 1990 Donetsk basin is to produce 193. 3 Mt, the Pechora basin 28. 3 Mt, the Kuznetsk basin 155 Mt, and Ekibastuz basin 95-96 Mt of coal. New machinery to be developed and new facilities to be built are described.

entry.dc:title: Integrated open-pit planning approach and systems.
entry.dc:creator: Mellish M.
entry.prism:publicationName: Mining Latin America Mineria Latinoamericana Papers Presented at the Conference Santiago 1986 Institution of Mining Metallurgy London Imm N American Publications Center Brookfield Vt
entry.dc:description: Rio Tinto Corporation Zinc PLC has major open pit mining interests around the world, all of which have been planned using computerised techniques. The successful project planning and detailed operational planning of many of these has been conducted using an integrated set of computer software which has been constantly improved over the last two decades. This paper is limited to consideration of large open pits although many aspects are also applicable to other types and sizes of operation. The approach is based on a geological and mining team effort with the geological and mining aspects being considered at all times. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: HIGHWALL STABILITY MONITORING AT SYNCRUDE CANADA LTD. OPEN PIT MINING OPERATION.
entry.dc:creator: Fair A.
entry.dc:description: The Syncrude Canada Ltd. open pit mine is located approximately 40 km north of Ft. McMurray in northern Alberta. The mining operation utilizes draglines to excavate the oil sands in a single bench operation with up to 60 meter high cuts. The permit level of daily production is 129,000 barrels of synthetic crude oil, and the mine production over the 25-year mine life is in the order of 265,000 tons per day. Since production startup in June 1977, potential slope instability problems have been identified that could affect the safety of the draglines. Four main types of instability have been identified to date. Of these, shallow block slides are considered to be the most hazardous and result from the presence of adversely dipping clay beds within the upper 20 m of the highwall face. The highwall monitoring techniques currently being utilized have evolved over the past 10 years, beginning with the original Test Pit program in 1973-74. Current routine monitoring methods involve vertical slope inclinometers and visual observation. These methods are intermittent and manpower intensive. A review of currently available monitoring methods has shown that traditional surface techniques are not feasible with Syncrude's current mining configuration.

entry.dc:title: Selection of a Method of Open Pit Mining Protection Against Groundwater as a Function of Hydrogeological Conditions.
entry.dc:creator: Mrsovic D.
entry.dc:description: The lignite deposit at Drmno belongs to the Kostolac Coal Basin. Extensive exploration works were completed, yielding hydrogeological relations and parameters of the Deposit. Two alternative protective solutions were proposed: well method, and a combined method (protective curtain, pre-dewatering cut, and wells). The advantage was given to the second which afforded improved operating effects and greater mining safety. Protective works were completed in three stages: preparation, opening, and full mining. The effects of the drainage system operation were monitored during all three operating stages.

entry.dc:title: DEVELOPMENT AND INTRODUCTION OF BOILERS BURNING KANSKACHINSK COAL AT THERMOELECTRIC POWER PLANTS.
entry.dc:creator: Boitsov Y.
entry.prism:publicationName: Soviet Energy Technology English Translation of Energomashinostroenie
entry.dc:description: It is known that the fuel balance of thermoelectric power plants is undergoing major changes: the consumption of fuel oil has declined, and the proportion of solid fuel has increased, especially in eastern regions of the USSR. In recent years, the use of eastern coal in has taken on steadily increasing importance in the country's fuel-energy balance. Most of the coal beds are shallow, which creates the conditions for open pit mining using high-speed mining techniques.

entry.dc:title: Problems of Intensification of Transportless Burden Removal Systems.
entry.dc:creator: Shchadov M.
entry.dc:description: By the year 2000, more than 50% of the total coal output of the USSR is to come from open pit mining. Intensification of open pit mining can be accomplished by means of effective 'transportless' burden removal systems by means of powerful walking excavators. This also means improvement of the stability of internal dump slopes, expecially those on an inclined base. By appropriate control, explosions can be utilized to shape dumps and to stabilize their slopes. The efficiency of operation of excavators is discussed. Some recommendations are offered.

entry.dc:title: STATUS OF OPEN PIT MINING IN THE FEDERAL REPUBLIC OF GERMANY.
entry.dc:creator: Jochums A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The historical development of open pit mining techniques in Germany which culminated in extraordinary technical advances after the Second World War and which found widespread recognition in other countries is reported. The high degree of mechanization is obligatory in Germany to stay within economic limits: the coal is of very poor quality and ranges from 1900-2300 kcal/kg; the deposits close to the surface have been exploited and present mining activities have reached more than 350 m depth from the surface; cost of labor is in the upper most bracket comparing industrialized nations in the world. Obviously, only mechanization and to some extent automization can provide the answer.

entry.dc:title: ASPECTS OF ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT FOR OPEN PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Streit E.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: Raw materials for basic industry and power generating plants are excavated in opencast mines by two different mining methods: continuous mining, employing bucket wheel excavators; and discontinuous mining (strip mining), employing draglines and shovels. Depending upon the geological structure of the mine a combination of both methods can also be used. The main equipment-groups for opencast mining are: bucket wheel excavator, conveyor system, tripper car and spreader. Since all these equipment are driven by electric motors, an extensive range of power equipment is necessary.

entry.dc:title: Application Fields in Open Pit Mining, Working Technologies and Parameter Calculation of the Explosive Charges Located in Chamber Holes.
entry.dc:creator: Muste I.
entry.dc:description: Blasting technology with explosive charges located in chamber holes in open pit mining, its applicability, the influence of certain physical and mechanical properties of the rocks and minerals, as well as the working technology and parameter calculation of the explosive charges located in the chamber holes are presented.

entry.dc:title: Shock airwaves in short-delayed blasting for open pit mining
entry.dc:creator: Ganopol'skii M.I.
entry.dc:description: 1. During a short delayed blasting with a delay interval between groups of 50 m/sec, a complete separation of SAW pulses produced by individual charges is observed. The weight of the charge in a group in that case can be taken equal to the weight that would be safe for an instant blasting. When the delay is 30 m/sec, the charge weight in a group should not exceed two-thirds, and for a delay of 20 m/sec a half, of the maximum admissible weight for instant blasting. These recommendations are applicable at distances not greater than 2000 m from the explosion site. 2. When blasting a linear string of charges, the delay interval at which SAW pulses are fully separated depends on the direction at which detonation propagates along the block and is defined by relations (13) and (14). With this position of charges, they should be detonated in the direction away from the object to be protected. © 1986 Plenum Publishing Corporation.

entry.dc:title: Conveyor technology reaches a peak.
entry.dc:creator: Smith A.
entry.dc:description: A review is presented on the present state of conveyor belt technology. The different types of materials and designs used are discussed: fabric belting; pipe conveying/air beds/steel; steel cord/aramid fibres; curving and incline belts. The market outlook is quoted as being bleak, but with possible demand for long distance conveying and specialised applications such as open pit mining. (A.J.)

entry.dc:title: APPLYING THE NEW ROBOTICS TO CONSTRUCTION AND AGRICULTURE.
entry.dc:creator: Leonard R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Technical Paper Society of Manufacturing Engineers
entry.dc:description: Recent advances in industrial automation, artificial intelligence and autonomous planetary rovers support a synthesis of these techniques to create mobile construction robots. These machines could perform repetitive tasks such as open pit mining, hot house harvesting of vegetables or mining the moon. A developmental program which solves immediate needs is outlined.

entry.dc:title: Possibilities for Underground Water Quality Prediction in Areas of Open Pit Brown Coal Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Hummel J.
entry.dc:description: The article describes the development of and the computer programs' efficiencies in simulation of the underground water quality in areas of brown coal open pit mining. The drainage of the open pits and hydrology of these areas are the main components in simulations and predictions of the underground water quality to ensure the healthy water supply to the residents of these areas.

entry.dc:title: Bingham Open Pit Mine of Kennecott Utah Copper Division/USA.
entry.dc:creator: Strzodka K.
entry.dc:description: The article reviews the local geology of the copper deposits and lead-zinc paragenesis and the open pit mining at the Bingham Mine.

entry.dc:title: First Industrial Robots in Brown Coal Open Pit Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Brueckel K.
entry.dc:description: The article describes the first industrial robot used in open pit mining of brown coal in the German Democratic Republic.

entry.dc:title: Concepts and Working Methods in Open Pits (I).
entry.dc:creator: Huidu E.
entry.dc:description: Up to now, the technical literature has not clarified the problems regarding the classification and the origin of the technological concepts related to the open pit mining. The authors review the following methods: conventional, European, American, combined, and hydraulic mining as well as special open pit mining methods. Examples are also given.

entry.dc:title: Mining of Oil Sands in Alberta, Canada.
entry.dc:creator: Golosinski T.
entry.dc:description: The article describes the mining of oil sands in Alberta, Canada. Open pit mining is described. The article reviews the geology of the mine and the excavating machinery which is used.

entry.dc:title: EUROPEAN BROWNCOAL MINING TO-DATE AND FUTURE TRENDS.
entry.dc:creator: Hagelueken M.
entry.prism:publicationName: Gluckauf Die Fachzeitschrift Fur Rohstoff Bergbau Und Energie
entry.dc:description: This survey deals with browncoal mining in all European countries except for the Soviet Union. For several of these - GDR, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, Bulgaria and Yugoslavia - browncoal is the major primary energy form. The survey indicates that major developments are in open pit mining. The mining costs are lower and safety is better in open pit operations than in underground mining. Refs.

entry.dc:title: Comparison of geostatistical calculations with the results of open pit mining at the Iharkut bauxite district, Hungary: A case study
entry.dc:creator: Bárdossy A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of the International Association for Mathematical Geology
entry.dc:description: Geostatistical calculations were carried out on two completely exhausted open-pit bauxite mines in the Iharkut bauxite district, Hungary. Fictitious regular drilling grids were laid on the maps, and horizontal variograms were calculated for drilling grids evaluating the bauxite surface, footwall surface, and bauxite thickness. Point kriging was carried out for all three parameters. Bauxite reserves were calculated using block kriging for bauxite thickness. The total estimation variance of the reserves has been established. Results were compared with real reserves obtained from the mine maps. © 1984 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
entry.authkeywords: bauxite prospecting | geostatistics | open-pit mining | reserve evaluation

entry.dc:title: BLUE RIDGE MINING TACKLES MAJOR PROJECT.
entry.dc:creator: Herod B.
entry.dc:description: A major realignment of mining and quarrying operations has been undertaken during the past year at the Luttrell, Tenn. , property of Penn-Virginia Limestone Corp. For many years, the high-quality limestone strata exposed here have been extracted to supply a lime kiln and grinding plant processing uncalcined chemical grade stone. Since the end of 1983, a program has been well underway that concentrated on developing open pit operations to the point where, in 6 months, most stone would be extracted from full time quarrying. The goal was met early in 1984, well ahead of schedule, and underground workings no longer are the primary source of raw material. The open pit mining operations are described in detail.
